title: Comparison of Relapse Risk Prediction Models During Active Surveillance in Stage I Seminoma: A Retrospective Multicenter Cohort Study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Comparison of Relapse Risk Prediction Models During Active Surveillance in Stage I Seminoma: A Retrospective Multicenter Cohort Study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】To improve the prediction of relapse for clinical stage I seminoma, we aimed to validate the Boormans model (incorporating tumor size, rete testis invasion, and lymphovascular invasion) against the conventional classification (tumor size > 4 cm/rete testis invasion).

evidence.text: To improve the prediction of relapse for clinical stage I seminoma, we aimed to validate the Boormans model (incorporating tumor size, rete testis invasion, and lymphovascular invasion) against the conventional classification (tumor size > 4 cm/rete testis invasion).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】Consecutive cSI seminoma patients managed with active surveillance after orchidectomy across multiple centers were retrospectively analyzed (1994-2024).

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】Part of the data was provided by the prospective Swiss-Austrian-German Testicular Cancer Cohort Study Group.

evidence.text: Consecutive cSI seminoma patients managed with active surveillance after orchidectomy across multiple centers were retrospectively analyzed (1994-2024).
Part of the data was provided by the prospective Swiss-Austrian-German Testicular Cancer Cohort Study Group.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Comparison of Relapse Risk Prediction Models During Active Surveillance in Stage I Seminoma: A Retrospective Multicenter Cohort Study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】Among the 1025 patients, 116 (11.3%) relapsed during a median follow-up of 45 months (95% CI 42-48).

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】In the descriptive multivariable analysis, TS (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.04) and RTI (HR 2.73, 95% CI 1.83-4.06) were found to be independent predictors of relapse.

evidence.text: Among the 1025 patients, 116 (11.3%) relapsed during a median follow-up of 45 months (95% CI 42-48).
In the descriptive multivariable analysis, TS (HR 1.03, 95% CI 1.01-1.04) and RTI (HR 2.73, 95% CI 1.83-4.06) were found to be independent predictors of relapse.
